drugs.name: Acyclovir
drugs.quickDose: NAG suspected HSV encephalitis: 10 mg/kg IV q8h; treatment duration commonly 14–21 days.
doseNotes: Adjust for renal impairment and ensure adequate hydration.
Obesity dosing weight should follow the source-specific rule.
warnings: Crystal nephropathy/neurotoxicity risk increases with renal dysfunction or inadequate adjustment.

precautions: Review renal/hepatic function and agent-specific interactions.
contraindications: Agent-specific contraindications apply.
interactions: Check current product information.

formulary.status: A* for 250 mg injection; oral formulations have formulation-specific categories.

drugs.name: Amikacin
drugs.quickDose: Weight-based aminoglycoside; dosing interval and redosing require renal/RRT assessment and TDM.
doseNotes: MSIC renal appendix gives RRT-specific regimens; use the TDM workspace for sampling reminders.
warnings: TDM and renal adjustment are essential.

clinicalProfile.mechanism: Aminoglycoside; 30S ribosomal inhibition with concentration-dependent killing.
adverseEffects: Nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, neuromuscular blockade.
precautions: TDM, renal/RRT adjustment and dosing weight are essential.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity; caution in neuromuscular disease.
interactions: Additive nephro/ototoxicity.

formulary.dose: Adult formulary: 15 mg/kg/day IM/IV in divided doses; max 1.5 g/day.
formulary.status: Selected fields verified against the live MOH FUKKM during this build. Recheck live before prescribing because formulary entries can change.

paediatric.dose: Child: 15 mg/kg/day in divided doses; neonate formulary entry includes a 10 mg/kg loading dose then 7.5 mg/kg q12h.
paediatric.note: FUKKM paediatric dose shown as a formulary cross-check. Use indication-specific paediatric guidance/local pharmacy policy where applicable.

preparation.reconstitution: Solution; no reconstitution required for the cited 250 mg/mL product.
preparation.dilution: Adult IV intermittent infusion: dilute in 100–200 mL compatible diluent; cited maximum concentration 5 mg/mL.
preparation.administration: Infuse over 30–60 min; infants may require longer infusion according to the protocol.
preparation.compatibility: Compatible diluents include NS, D5, NSD5 and LR. Separate administration from penicillins/cephalosporins rather than mixing in the same solution.

drugs.name: Amoxicillin
drugs.quickDose: Indication-specific. Common NAG oral regimens include 500–1000 mg PO q8h; use the linked syndrome/source card.
doseNotes: Dose and duration are syndrome-specific; renal adjustment may be required.
warnings: Do not use when β-lactamase-producing pathogens are likely unless susceptibility supports it.

clinicalProfile.mechanism: Binds penicillin-binding proteins and inhibits bacterial peptidoglycan cell-wall synthesis.
adverseEffects: Hypersensitivity; gastrointestinal upset; antibiotic-associated diarrhoea/C. difficile can occur.
precautions: Review immediate/severe β-lactam allergy history; adjust renally eliminated agents when indicated.
contraindications: Serious immediate hypersensitivity to the product/class.
interactions: Drug-specific interactions and compatibility vary; check the product label and pharmacy policy.

formulary.status: B for 250 mg/500 mg capsules and listed oral solutions.

drugs.name: Amoxicillin–Clavulanate
drugs.quickDose: Common adult IV regimen in the source set: 1.2 g q8h; some intra-abdominal/abscess indications use q6h.
doseNotes: Use syndrome-specific regimen and renal adjustment.
warnings: No Pseudomonas coverage.

drugs.name: Amphotericin B deoxycholate
drugs.quickDose: Indication-specific weight-based IV therapy; NAG cryptococcal/histoplasmosis regimens use source-specific 0.7–1 mg/kg/day ranges.
doseNotes: Use the exact syndrome card; formulation matters.
warnings: Nephrotoxicity, electrolyte loss and infusion reactions require active monitoring.

adverseEffects: Infusion reactions, nephrotoxicity and potassium/magnesium wasting are clinically important.
precautions: Monitor renal function, potassium, magnesium and infusion tolerance.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to the product; formulation-specific issues apply.
interactions: Additive nephrotoxicity and electrolyte-mediated arrhythmia risk with interacting drugs.

formulary.status: A for conventional amphotericin B 50 mg injection.

drugs.name: Ampicillin
drugs.quickDose: Common high-severity regimens use 2 g IV q4–6h; meningitis/Listeria coverage uses 2 g IV q4h in NAG/HPUSM pathways.
doseNotes: NAG acute meningitis: 2 g IV q4h when Listeria coverage is indicated.
MSIC renal appendix: higher doses may be used in bacteraemia, endocarditis, meningitis and obesity; maintenance is renal/RRT adjusted.
warnings: Adjust maintenance dose in renal impairment.

precautions: Review immediate/severe β-lactam allergy history; adjust renally eliminated agents when indicated.

interactions: Drug-specific interactions and compatibility vary; check the product label and pharmacy policy.

formulary.status: B for 500 mg injection and listed oral suspension.

drugs.name: Ampicillin–Sulbactam
drugs.quickDose: For susceptible Acinetobacter: 3 g IV q6h; high-dose sulbactam regimens are used for CRAB in local/MDR guidance.
doseNotes: MSIC renal appendix lists 3 g q6h for Acinetobacter and 9 g q8h over 4 h for carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter.
Local HPUSM targeted CRAB guidance includes high-dose extended infusion in moderate–severe infection.
drugs.pkpd: Time-dependent β-lactam; high-dose sulbactam exposure is the key CRAB concept.
warnings: Does not cover Pseudomonas.
CRAB therapy should be checked against dedicated MDR guidance and susceptibility data.

drugs.name: Anidulafungin
drugs.quickDose: MSIC invasive candidiasis: 200 mg IV loading dose then 100 mg IV q24h.
doseNotes: MSIC obesity appendix increases loading/maintenance by 25% when ABW ≥140 kg.

clinicalProfile.mechanism: Inhibits fungal β-(1,3)-D-glucan synthesis, weakening the fungal cell wall.
adverseEffects: Infusion reactions and hepatic enzyme abnormalities may occur.
precautions: Review hepatic function and infusion reactions; agent-specific interactions vary.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to the product.
interactions: Agent-specific; check current product information.

formulary.status: A* for 100 mg injection.

drugs.name: Artesunate
drugs.quickDose: MSIC severe malaria: 2.4 mg/kg IV at 0, 12 and 24 h, then q24h while parenteral treatment is required; follow the full malaria regimen/source.
doseNotes: Transition to oral ACT when clinically appropriate per guideline.
warnings: Delayed haemolysis monitoring after IV artesunate may be relevant.

clinicalProfile.mechanism: Mechanism is agent/class specific; see source references.
adverseEffects: Delayed haemolysis monitoring after IV artesunate may be relevant.
precautions: Use indication-, host- and source-specific precautions.
contraindications: Check current product information and local formulary.
interactions: Check current product information.

drugs.name: Azithromycin
drugs.quickDose: Severe CAP regimens in the source set commonly use 500 mg IV/PO q24h as atypical coverage.
doseNotes: Duration varies by syndrome and confirmed pathogen.
drugs.pkpd: Useful for atypical respiratory pathogens; not a broad Gram-negative ICU agent.
warnings: Consider QT interval and interacting QT-prolonging drugs.

clinicalProfile.mechanism: Binds the 50S ribosomal subunit and inhibits bacterial protein synthesis.
adverseEffects: Gastrointestinal effects, hepatotoxicity and QT prolongation are important class effects.
precautions: Review QT risk, electrolytes and hepatic dysfunction.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity; drug-specific contraindications vary.
interactions: Many macrolides have clinically important CYP/P-gp interactions; azithromycin has fewer CYP interactions than clarithromycin/erythromycin.

formulary.status: A* for 500 mg injection; A/KK for listed oral formulations.

drugs.name: Aztreonam
drugs.quickDose: Specialist MDR role, especially paired with ceftazidime–avibactam for selected MBL/NDM CRE in MSIDC guidance.
doseNotes: MSIDC: ceftazidime–avibactam + aztreonam is a preferred strategy for selected MBL/NDM CRE outside urinary tract.
warnings: Do not infer MBL activity from aztreonam alone; co-produced serine β-lactamases can inactivate it.

clinicalProfile.mechanism: Monobactam β-lactam with predominant Gram-negative activity; binds PBPs and inhibits cell-wall synthesis.
adverseEffects: Hypersensitivity, gastrointestinal/hepatic laboratory abnormalities and local infusion reactions can occur.
precautions: Renal dose adjustment is required; carefully review ceftazidime allergy because of the shared side-chain issue in clinical allergy assessment.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to aztreonam/product components.
interactions: Do not co-administer in the same line with known incompatible drugs without flushing/compatibility confirmation.

formulary.status: Check live MOH MyFormulary for the exact formulation, prescriber category and restriction.

preparation.reconstitution: For infusion, the cited label initially reconstitutes each gram with at least 3 mL sterile water; for bolus injection, 6–10 mL sterile water is used.
preparation.dilution: Further dilute in a compatible infusion solution; cited label lists 0.9% sodium chloride, dextrose and several balanced solutions.
preparation.administration: Intermittent infusion is completed over 20–60 min in the product label; MSIDC NDM regimens in AbxHub may specify prolonged administration.
preparation.compatibility: Known incompatibilities exist; flush shared tubing before/after incompatible agents.

drugs.name: Benzylpenicillin
drugs.quickDose: Severe leptospirosis: 1.5 million units IV q6h in HPUSM/MSIC/NAG pathways; other indications use source-specific high-dose regimens.
doseNotes: NAG severe leptospirosis: 1.5 MU IV q6h.
MSIC renal appendix: usual 2–4 MU q4–6h with renal/RRT adjustment.

formulary.status: B for 1 mega unit and 5 mega unit injections.

drugs.quickDose: MSIC invasive candidiasis: 70 mg IV loading dose then 50 mg IV q24h.
doseNotes: Use syndrome-specific guidance for step-down and duration.

drugs.name: Cefazolin
drugs.quickDose: 2 g IV q6–8h appears in NAG bone/joint pathways; dose adjust in renal impairment.
doseNotes: NAG acute osteomyelitis alternative: cefazolin 2 g IV q6–8h.
MSIC renal appendix: normal dose 2 g q8h with renal/RRT adjustment.

clinicalProfile.mechanism: Binds penicillin-binding proteins and inhibits bacterial peptidoglycan cell-wall synthesis.

formulary.indications: Susceptible infections including respiratory, urogenital, SSTI, biliary, bone/joint, endocarditis, sepsis and surgical prophylaxis
formulary.dose: Adult formulary: 500–1000 mg 2–4 times daily depending on severity; life-threatening infection may use higher doses.
formulary.status: Selected fields verified against the live MOH FUKKM during this build. Recheck live before prescribing because formulary entries can change.

paediatric.dose: Children >1 month: 25–50 mg/kg/day in 3–4 divided doses in the cited formulary entry.
paediatric.note: FUKKM paediatric dose shown as a formulary cross-check. Use indication-specific paediatric guidance/local pharmacy policy where applicable.

drugs.name: Cefepime
drugs.quickDose: MSIC ICU: LD 2 g IV, then 1–2 g q8–12h over 4 h; severe pneumonia commonly uses 2 g q8h.
doseNotes: Higher dose is used in bacteraemia, endocarditis, meningitis and severe pneumonia in the MSIC renal appendix.
Renal adjustment is important because accumulation increases neurotoxicity risk.
drugs.pkpd: Time-dependent β-lactam; extended infusion supports fT>MIC target attainment.
warnings: MSIC notes higher neurotoxicity risk in elderly patients, renal impairment and inappropriate dosing.
No reliable anaerobic coverage; add an anaerobic agent when the syndrome requires it.

clinicalProfile.mechanism: Fourth-generation cephalosporin β-lactam that binds PBPs and inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis.
adverseEffects: Neurotoxicity (encephalopathy, myoclonus/seizures) is a key concern with renal dysfunction/excess exposure; hypersensitivity and C. difficile can occur.
precautions: Adjust for renal function and reassess promptly if new altered mental status/myoclonus develops.
contraindications: Serious immediate hypersensitivity to cefepime/cephalosporins or product components.
interactions: Review nephrotoxic co-medications and admixture compatibility.

formulary.indications: Febrile neutropenia, septicaemia, lower respiratory, urinary, skin/structure, gynaecologic and intra-abdominal infections
formulary.dose: Adult formulary: 1–2 g twice daily for most infections; severe/febrile neutropenia 2 g three times daily.
formulary.status: Selected fields verified against the live MOH FUKKM during this build. Recheck live before prescribing because formulary entries can change.

preparation.reconstitution: For IV use, cited protocol: 500 mg vial + 5 mL or 1 g vial + 10 mL WFI/NS/D5.
preparation.dilution: Further dilute to 50–100 mL for intermittent infusion; cited maximum infusion concentration 40 mg/mL.
preparation.administration: IV bolus 3–5 min or intermittent infusion about 30 min; extended infusion may be used when clinically indicated.
preparation.compatibility: Compatible diluents include D5 and NS; do not mix with gentamicin, metronidazole, vancomycin, tobramycin or netilmicin in the cited protocol.

paediatric.dose: Age 2 months–16 years and ≤40 kg: 50 mg/kg q8–12h for 7–10 days in the cited formulary entry.
paediatric.note: FUKKM paediatric dose shown as a formulary cross-check. Use indication-specific paediatric guidance/local pharmacy policy where applicable.

drugs.name: Cefiderocol
drugs.quickDose: MSIDC MDR guidance: 2 g IV q8h in normal renal function; dose increases with augmented clearance and decreases with renal impairment.
doseNotes: Use only for source-supported resistant Gram-negative indications with susceptibility and specialist review.
drugs.pkpd: Time-dependent β-lactam exposure; prolonged infusion is used in MDR guidance.
warnings: Dedicated MDR guidance and AST should direct use.

clinicalProfile.mechanism: Binds PBPs and inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis.
adverseEffects: Hypersensitivity, gastrointestinal effects and C. difficile; neurotoxicity can occur with high exposure, especially in renal dysfunction.
precautions: Renal dose adjustment and neurotoxicity surveillance are important for renally eliminated agents such as cefepime.
contraindications: Serious immediate hypersensitivity to the product/class.
interactions: Drug-specific compatibility and anticoagulation interactions vary; check current product information.

formulary.status: Check live MOH MyFormulary for the exact formulation, prescriber category and restriction.

drugs.name: Cefotaxime
drugs.quickDose: CNS and severe systemic regimens are indication-specific; NAG meningitis uses 2 g IV q6h as an alternative to ceftriaxone.
doseNotes: NAG acute meningitis alternative: cefotaxime 2 g IV q6h + ampicillin when Listeria coverage is indicated.
NAG urosepsis without shock: cefotaxime 2 g IV q8h is a preferred option.

drugs.name: Ceftazidime
drugs.quickDose: MSIC ICU: LD 2 g IV, then 1–2 g q8h over 4 h; melioidosis/higher MIC regimen uses 2 g q6h over 4 h.
doseNotes: Renal dose adjustment is required.
Current NAG severe CAP page states ceftazidime is not recommended for empirical CAP because of poor pneumococcal activity.
drugs.pkpd: Time-dependent β-lactam; prolonged infusion is used in MSIC ICU dosing.
warnings: Do not infer pneumococcal coverage from “third-generation cephalosporin” label; syndrome-specific guidance matters.

clinicalProfile.mechanism: Third-generation antipseudomonal cephalosporin; binds PBPs and inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis.
adverseEffects: Hypersensitivity, gastrointestinal effects/C. difficile and neurotoxicity with excessive exposure, especially in renal dysfunction.
precautions: Adjust for renal function; use source-specific high-dose/prolonged infusion for melioidosis/MDR contexts only when indicated.
contraindications: Serious immediate hypersensitivity to ceftazidime/cephalosporins or product components.
interactions: Do not admix ceftazidime and aminoglycosides in the same solution because of potential physical/chemical interaction.

formulary.dose: Adult formulary: 1 g q8h or 2 g q12h; severe infection 2 g q8h.
formulary.status: Selected fields verified against the live MOH FUKKM during this build. Recheck live before prescribing because formulary entries can change.

preparation.reconstitution: Cited 2 g vial: add 10 mL WFI, giving approximately 170 mg/mL after reconstitution.
preparation.dilution: For intermittent infusion, further dilute to 50–100 mL; cited maximum 40 mg/mL.
preparation.administration: IV bolus 3–5 min or intermittent infusion 15–30 min; extended infusion can also be used.
preparation.compatibility: NS, D5 and Hartmann-type diluent are listed. Avoid sodium bicarbonate as diluent; flush line between ceftazidime and vancomycin.

paediatric.dose: Child: 25–150 mg/kg/day in 2–3 divided doses in the cited formulary entry.
paediatric.note: FUKKM paediatric dose shown as a formulary cross-check. Use indication-specific paediatric guidance/local pharmacy policy where applicable.

drugs.name: Ceftazidime–Avibactam
drugs.quickDose: Dedicated MDR option for selected CRE/DTR Pseudomonas when susceptibility/mechanism support activity.
doseNotes: MSIDC CRE guidance uses ceftazidime–avibactam as a preferred option for susceptible carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales outside the urinary tract.
For MBL/NDM CRE, MSIDC uses ceftazidime–avibactam together with aztreonam rather than ceftazidime–avibactam alone.
drugs.pkpd: Time-dependent β-lactam exposure; activity depends strongly on β-lactamase mechanism.
warnings: Carbapenemase mechanism matters; not active alone against metallo-β-lactamases.

clinicalProfile.mechanism: Ceftazidime inhibits PBPs/cell-wall synthesis; avibactam inhibits selected serine β-lactamases but does not directly inhibit metallo-β-lactamases.
adverseEffects: Hypersensitivity, gastrointestinal effects/C. difficile and CNS effects with excessive β-lactam exposure are relevant.
precautions: Renal dose adjustment is important; mechanism of carbapenemase matters because NDM/MBL requires a different strategy.
contraindications: Serious hypersensitivity to ceftazidime-avibactam/cephalosporins or product components.
interactions: Check renal-function changes and product-specific interactions; use MSIDC guidance for simultaneous aztreonam in NDM/MBL infection.

formulary.indications: Complicated intra-abdominal infection (with metronidazole), complicated UTI/pyelonephritis, HAP/VAP
formulary.restriction: Restricted to CRE as polymyxin-sparing option; start after proven susceptibility; Infectious Disease Specialist only.
formulary.dose: 2.5 g (ceftazidime 2 g/avibactam 0.5 g) q8h by IV infusion over 2 h for 5–14 days in the cited formulary entry.
formulary.status: Selected fields verified against the live MOH FUKKM during this build. Recheck live before prescribing because formulary entries can change.

preparation.reconstitution: The cited 2.5 g vial is constituted with 10 mL of an approved diluent; the resulting solution must be further diluted before infusion.
preparation.dilution: For a 2.5 g adult dose, withdraw the full constituted vial and dilute to 50–250 mL with an approved infusion diluent; smaller renal-adjusted doses use proportionally smaller withdrawal volumes.
preparation.administration: Use the regimen/infusion duration specified by the resistance and renal source card; MSIDC uses prolonged infusion in its MDR table.
preparation.compatibility: For NDM therapy, MSIDC states ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam should be administered simultaneously and notes Y-site compatibility.

MSIDC dedicated DTR Pseudomonas guidance lists ceftolozane–tazobactam among preferred newer β-lactam options when active.

warnings: Use susceptibility and dedicated MDR guidance; renal adjustment is required.

formulary.restriction: Carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas as polymyxin-sparing treatment; susceptibility required for nosocomial pneumonia; ID Specialist only.
formulary.dose: 1.5 g q8h for cIAI/cUTI; 3 g q8h for nosocomial pneumonia in the cited formulary entry.

doseNotes: Select dose by indication rather than using a single universal regimen.
warnings: No Pseudomonas coverage.
Avoid treating AmpC-risk organisms solely from a generic susceptible report without considering inducible resistance and syndrome.

paediatric.note: FUKKM paediatric dose shown as a formulary cross-check. Use indication-specific paediatric guidance/local pharmacy policy where applicable.

drugs.name: Cefuroxime
drugs.quickDose: Common inpatient dose 750 mg–1.5 g IV q8h depending on syndrome; renal adjustment applies.
doseNotes: HPUSM pyelonephritis: 750–1500 mg IV q8h as an alternative.
NAG complicated UTI: 750–1500 mg IV q8h is an alternative.

adverseEffects: Hypersensitivity, gastrointestinal effects, cytopenias and electrolyte/sodium-related issues can occur; renal toxicity risk requires clinical context.

contraindications: Serious hypersensitivity to penicillins/cephalosporins/β-lactamase inhibitors or product components.

doseNotes: Normal renal function: 15–20 mg/kg q12h after loading dose in the MSIC TDM appendix.
AUC24/MIC target 400–600 is shown in the MSIC hypoalbuminaemia appendix; trough 15–20 mg/L is an alternate exposure indicator in selected contexts.
Infusion rate should not exceed 10 mg/min.
drugs.pkpd: Exposure-dependent killing; AUC-guided monitoring is preferred where feasible.
warnings: TDM is required for serious infections and changing renal function.
Vancomycin is inferior to antistaphylococcal β-lactams for MSSA when those agents can be used.

clinicalProfile.mechanism: Glycopeptide that binds D-Ala-D-Ala cell-wall precursors and inhibits Gram-positive cell-wall synthesis.
adverseEffects: Nephrotoxicity and infusion reactions are major concerns; cytopenias and ototoxicity can occur.
precautions: Use AUC/TDM-guided dosing for serious systemic infection where feasible; adjust to renal/RRT status and avoid excessive infusion rates.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to vancomycin/product components.
interactions: Additive nephro/ototoxicity with other toxic agents; review concurrent piperacillin-tazobactam/nephrotoxin exposure and local evidence/policy.

formulary.indications: Susceptible Gram-positive infection where alternatives are unsuitable, including MRSA/Enterococcus; severe staphylococcal infection when penicillins/cephalosporins cannot be used

doseNotes: TDM and interaction review are important for prolonged treatment.

warnings: Visual/hepatic toxicity and multiple CYP interactions; review QT risk.

conditions.name: Acute Appendicitis / Appendiceal Infection
conditions.summary: Source control defines the antibiotic course; postoperative antibiotics can often stop after adequate source control in uncomplicated disease.
before: Assess uncomplicated vs perforated/abscess disease
Obtain surgical source-control plan

recommendations.label: Non-operative uncomplicated pathway
preferred: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q6h
alternative: Use source-listed alternative if allergy/resistance changes choice
recommendations.duration: NAG non-operative pathway uses a multi-day course; tailor to response.

recommendations.label: After adequate appendectomy/source control
preferred: Stop antimicrobials when uncomplicated appendicitis has definitive source control and no ongoing infection indication
recommendations.duration: Complicated disease generally receives a short post-source-control course, guided by response.

why: Duration should follow source control rather than an automatic prolonged course.

conditions.name: Acute Bacterial Prostatitis
conditions.summary: Choose oral vs IV therapy by severity and culture, with antipseudomonal coverage when risk factors are present.
before: Obtain appropriate microbiology before antimicrobial therapy when this will not cause harmful delay
Review previous cultures and recent antimicrobial exposure
Check allergy, renal function and interacting/toxic co-medications
Assess source control and severity
Avoid prostatic massage in acute severe infection
Assess retention/abscess and need for urologic intervention

recommendations.label: Outpatient / stable
preferred: Ciprofloxacin 500–750 mg PO q12h when susceptible and appropriate
alternative: Use culture-directed alternative from NAG/local susceptibility
recommendations.duration: Minimum 10–14 days; may extend up to 6 weeks depending on severity/response.

recommendations.label: Inpatient / severe
preferred: Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q12h OR amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q6h OR other source-listed agent based on culture
alternative: Ceftazidime 2 g IV q8h when Pseudomonas risk is clinically important
recommendations.duration: 10–14 days minimum; tailor to response and complications.

why: Prostatic penetration and complication assessment are more important than a generic UTI regimen.

conditions.name: Acute Cholangitis
conditions.summary: Urgent biliary drainage/source control is central; antimicrobial breadth follows severity/acquisition/resistance risk.
before: Assess for urgent biliary drainage
Obtain blood cultures in sepsis before therapy when feasible
Review prior biliary procedures and resistant organisms

recommendations.label: Community acquired / non-sepsis
preferred: Amoxicillin–clavulanate or ampicillin–sulbactam source-specific regimen
alternative: Third-generation cephalosporin ± metronidazole according to source/context
recommendations.duration: Usually 4–7 days; may be shorter after successful drainage and rapid fever resolution.

recommendations.label: Sepsis / complicated / hospital acquired
preferred: Piperacillin–tazobactam source-specific regimen
alternative: Broaden according to AMR risk and culture/susceptibility
recommendations.duration: Source-control dependent; generally 4–7 days after adequate drainage.

conditions.name: Acute Cholecystitis
conditions.summary: Severity and source control determine need, spectrum and duration. Carbapenems are reserved for high AMR risk/biliary instrumentation.
before: Assess sepsis/organ failure or perforation/abscess
Plan definitive biliary source control
Obtain cultures in severe/complicated disease where appropriate

recommendations.label: Non-sepsis
preferred: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q6h OR ampicillin–sulbactam 1.5–3 g IV q6h
alternative: Third-generation cephalosporin options according to source
recommendations.duration: Usually 4–7 days; selected mild/moderate cases may stop within 24 h after uncomplicated source control.

recommendations.label: Sepsis / organ failure / complicated
preferred: Piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6–8h
alternative: Reserve carbapenem for high AMR risk/history of biliary instrumentation rather than routine use.
recommendations.duration: Usually 4–7 days; q8h piperacillin–tazobactam as 3–4 h extended infusion.

conditions.name: Acute Diverticulitis
conditions.summary: Uncomplicated immunocompetent non-septic diverticulitis may not require antibiotics; systemic illness/complication changes the pathway.
before: Classify uncomplicated vs complicated disease
Assess sepsis/organ failure and source-control requirement

recommendations.label: Uncomplicated, immunocompetent, non-septic
preferred: Antibiotics may be omitted when the NAG criteria for uncomplicated disease are satisfied
recommendations.duration: Clinical observation/supportive care when antibiotics are not indicated.

recommendations.label: Systemic signs / higher risk
preferred: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q6h OR ampicillin–sulbactam 1.5–3 g IV q6h
alternative: Cefuroxime 1.5 g IV q8h + metronidazole
recommendations.duration: Usually 7–10 days total IV/PO in the cited pathway; reassess source control.

why: Antibiotic exposure can be avoided in carefully selected uncomplicated cases.

conditions.name: Acute Pharyngitis / Tonsillitis
conditions.summary: Use clinical scoring to avoid antibiotics for likely viral sore throat and reserve narrow-spectrum treatment for patients meeting bacterial-treatment criteria.
before: Assess Modified Centor or current NAG clinical pathway
Check allergy and features of deep-neck/peritonsillar complication

recommendations.label: Modified Centor <3
preferred: No antibiotic; provide symptomatic treatment
recommendations.duration: No antimicrobial course.

recommendations.label: Modified Centor ≥3 / likely GAS
preferred: Phenoxymethylpenicillin (Penicillin V) 500 mg PO q6h OR 1 g PO q12h
alternative: Use current NAG allergy alternative when penicillin cannot be used
recommendations.duration: Use the current NAG course for confirmed/likely GAS pharyngitis.

why: Most sore throats are viral; clinical scoring reduces unnecessary antimicrobial exposure.

conditions.name: Acute Pyelonephritis
conditions.summary: Obtain urine culture before treatment where possible and distinguish uncomplicated from complicated UTI/urosepsis.
before: Urinalysis and urine culture
Blood cultures if systemically unwell
Assess obstruction/stone and need for urgent source control
Check renal function and pregnancy status

recommendations.label: Local adult pyelonephritis
preferred: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q6h + gentamicin 5 mg/kg/24h
alternative: Cefuroxime 750–1500 mg IV q8h
recommendations.duration: 7 days

recommendations.label: Complicated UTI / pyelonephritis
preferred: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q6–8h OR ampicillin–sulbactam 1.5–3 g IV q6h; may add an aminoglycoside when indicated
alternative: Cefuroxime 750–1500 mg IV q8h
Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h
Ceftazidime 2 g IV q8h
recommendations.duration: Usually 5–7 days; step down when afebrile >48 h, clinically improving and able to take oral therapy.

conditions.diseaseMechanism: Most bacterial pyelonephritis is an ascending infection from the lower urinary tract; obstruction, stones, catheters and resistant colonisation increase complexity.

conditions.name: Aspiration Pneumonia
conditions.summary: Distinguish aspiration pneumonitis from bacterial aspiration infection; syndrome and healthcare exposure determine whether broad Gram-negative/anaerobic coverage is needed.
before: Obtain appropriate cultures before antimicrobials when this does not cause harmful delay
Review previous microbiology and recent antimicrobial exposure
Check allergy and previous serious antimicrobial adverse reactions
Check renal function and whether renal replacement therapy is being used
Assess for abscess/empyema and need for drainage
Clarify community vs healthcare-associated aspiration

recommendations.label: Local aspiration pneumonia
preferred: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q8h
alternative: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h ± metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h
recommendations.duration: Use clinical context; distinguish from lung abscess duration

recommendations.label: Healthcare-associated aspiration / lung abscess
preferred: Piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6h OR cefepime 2 g IV q8h + metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h
alternative: Meropenem 1 g IV q8h OR imipenem 500 mg IV q6h
recommendations.duration: Aspiration pneumonia 7 days; lung abscess minimum 4 weeks

recommendations.label: Aspiration pneumonia (not chemical pneumonitis)
preferred: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q8h
alternative: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h ± metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h when anaerobic coverage is specifically indicated
β-lactam allergy: clindamycin 600 mg IV/PO q8h
recommendations.duration: 7 days. Routine anaerobic coverage is not required unless lung abscess/empyema is suspected.

conditions.name: Bacterial Meningitis
conditions.summary: Time-critical syndrome: obtain blood cultures/CSF when safe without delaying treatment. Dose selection must achieve CNS exposure.
before: Obtain blood cultures promptly
Perform lumbar puncture when safe; do not delay time-critical antimicrobials for prolonged investigations
Assess need for imaging before LP based on neurological features
Consider age/immunocompromise and Listeria risk

recommendations.label: Adult empirical local regimen
preferred: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q12h + ampicillin 2 g IV q4h
alternative: Use allergy/pathogen-specific regimen
recommendations.duration: 7–21 days depending on organism/clinical context
notes: Dexamethasone 0.15 mg/kg q6h for 2–4 days is listed in the source.

recommendations.label: Adult acute bacterial meningitis — empirical
preferred: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q12h + ampicillin 2 g IV q4h when Listeria coverage is indicated
alternative: Cefotaxime 2 g IV q6h + ampicillin 2 g IV q4h
Severe cephalosporin allergy: consider meropenem 2 g IV q8h
recommendations.duration: If no organism is isolated but CSF supports bacterial meningitis and patient responds: 10–14 days; organism-specific durations supersede.

why: CNS dosing differs from routine dosing because adequate CSF/tissue exposure is required.
conditions.diseaseMechanism: Bacterial meningitis follows bloodstream or contiguous spread across CNS barriers, with meningeal inflammation driving cerebral oedema, impaired perfusion and neurological injury.

conditions.name: Bite-Related Wound Infection / Prophylaxis
conditions.summary: Irrigation/debridement and exposure-specific prophylaxis are central; antibiotic choice depends on bite source and contamination.
before: Copious irrigation and wound debridement
Assess rabies/tetanus and specific animal exposure risks
Evaluate tendon/joint/bone involvement

recommendations.label: Dog/cat/human and similar mammalian bites
preferred: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 625 mg PO q8h or 1.2 g IV q8h, depending on severity
alternative: Cefuroxime or ceftriaxone + metronidazole; doxycycline + metronidazole in selected allergy contexts
recommendations.duration: Prophylaxis commonly 3 days; established infection commonly 5 days, extended for deep complications.

recommendations.label: Macaque/monkey exposure
preferred: Follow the bite regimen and assess B-virus exposure; NAG includes acyclovir prophylaxis in selected macaque exposure contexts
recommendations.duration: Exposure-specific; check live NAG.

why: Wound care and zoonotic prophylaxis can be more important than simply choosing a broad antibiotic.

conditions.name: Brain Abscess
conditions.summary: Treat with prolonged therapy plus source control/neurosurgical assessment when indicated.
before: Obtain blood cultures and neurosurgical/microbiology specimens when feasible
Assess contiguous ENT/dental source, haematogenous source and prior neurosurgery
Plan source control/drainage where appropriate

recommendations.label: Local empirical regimen
preferred: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q12h + metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h
alternative: Cefotaxime 2 g IV q4–6h + metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h
recommendations.duration: 4–8 weeks; source lists minimum 2 weeks IV

recommendations.label: Brain abscess / subdural empyema — common oral/sinus/haematogenous sources
preferred: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q12h OR cefotaxime 2 g IV q4–6h, PLUS metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h
alternative: Otogenic/healthcare-associated pathways require source-specific antipseudomonal and staphylococcal coverage
recommendations.duration: Duration and source control are site/organism dependent; use the live NAG CNS section.

conditions.name: Cellulitis
conditions.summary: HPUSM ASP 2025 stratifies cellulitis by severity and primarily targets staphylococci and streptococci.
before: Assess severity and systemic toxicity
Look for abscess/necrotising infection or another source requiring drainage/source control
Review allergy history and renal function if IV broad-spectrum therapy is being considered

recommendations.label: Mild
preferred: Cloxacillin 500 mg PO q6h
alternative: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 625 mg PO q8h
recommendations.duration: 5–10 days

recommendations.label: Moderate
preferred: Cloxacillin 500 mg PO q6h
alternative: Ampicillin–sulbactam 3 g IV q6–8h
recommendations.duration: 7 days

recommendations.label: Severe
preferred: Piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6–8h
alternative: Ampicillin–sulbactam 3 g IV q6–8h
recommendations.duration: 7 days

recommendations.label: Severe cellulitis
preferred: Piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6–8h while severe/deep infection is being assessed, then de-escalate when cultures and exclusion of necrotising infection permit
alternative: Ampicillin–sulbactam 3 g IV q6h OR amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q8h; allergy pathway is source-specific
recommendations.duration: Usually 5–10 days based on response; q8h piperacillin–tazobactam should be infused over 3–4 h.

why: Severe disease broadens empirical coverage; abscess or necrotising infection requires a different pathway.

conditions.name: Central Line-Associated Bloodstream Infection / CRBSI
conditions.summary: HPUSM provides local empirical options for central-catheter and haemodialysis-catheter infection; definitive duration depends on the organism and catheter strategy.
before: Obtain blood cultures before antibiotics when feasible
Identify catheter type and assess whether catheter removal is required
Review prior microbiology and MRSA/MDR risk
Check renal function before vancomycin/ceftazidime dosing

recommendations.label: Central catheter
preferred: Cloxacillin 2 g IV q4–6h
recommendations.duration: 7–10 days in the local table; definitive duration depends on organism and clinical context.

recommendations.label: Haemodialysis catheter / MRSA-risk context
preferred: Vancomycin 15–20 mg/kg IV PLUS ceftazidime 2 g IV q24h
recommendations.duration: 10–14 days in the local table; duration depends on organism isolated from blood culture.
notes: Local table suggests catheter removal.

recommendations.label: Non-tunnelled central venous catheter / PICC — national empirical pathway
preferred: Cloxacillin 2 g IV q4–6h OR cefazolin 2 g IV q8h; may add ceftazidime 2 g IV q8h for Gram-negative coverage if critically ill or with femoral lines
alternative: If MRSA risk: vancomycin 15–20 mg/kg IV q8–12h; if prior ESBL colonisation/infection and severely/critically ill: meropenem 2 g IV q8h OR imipenem 1 g IV q8h
recommendations.duration: Depends on organism, catheter removal and complications; NAG suggests ID consultation.
notes: Obtain both peripheral and central-line blood cultures when CRBSI is suspected.
Catheter removal is recommended in the NAG pathway.

why: Device/source control and pathogen-specific therapy are central to management.

conditions.name: Cholera
conditions.summary: Aggressive rehydration is the main treatment; antimicrobials shorten illness in selected patients.
before: Start rapid oral/IV fluid and electrolyte replacement
Assess outbreak/travel context and obtain stool testing when indicated

recommendations.label: Antimicrobial option
preferred: Doxycycline 300 mg PO single dose
alternative: Ciprofloxacin 1 g PO single dose OR azithromycin 1 g PO single dose; erythromycin is another source-listed option
recommendations.duration: Single-dose regimens for selected agents; hydration remains the primary therapy.

why: Mortality is prevented primarily by rapid volume/electrolyte replacement.

conditions.name: Chronic Bacterial Prostatitis
conditions.summary: Requires a prolonged prostate-penetrating, susceptibility-directed regimen.
before: Obtain urine/culture evidence when possible
Review STI/atypical pathogen context and prior courses

recommendations.label: Culture-directed treatment
preferred: Ciprofloxacin 500–750 mg PO q12h when susceptible
alternative: Trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole 160/800 mg PO q12h; doxycycline/azithromycin only for specific source-listed pathogens
recommendations.duration: Typically 4–6 weeks; TMP-SMX courses may be longer in the source pathway.

why: Short courses have a high relapse risk because prostatic infection is difficult to eradicate.

conditions.name: Clostridioides difficile Infection
conditions.summary: Stop unnecessary inciting antimicrobials when possible and classify severity; fulminant disease requires high-dose oral vancomycin plus IV metronidazole in the NAG pathway.
before: Stop or narrow inciting antimicrobial when clinically feasible
Assess WCC, creatinine, shock, ileus and megacolon
Institute infection-control precautions according to local policy

recommendations.label: Initial non-severe / severe
preferred: Vancomycin 125 mg PO q6h
alternative: Non-severe only: metronidazole 400 mg PO q8h if vancomycin unavailable
recommendations.duration: 10 days.

recommendations.label: Fulminant colitis
preferred: Vancomycin 500 mg PO q6h PLUS metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h
recommendations.duration: Urgent reassessment and source-control/surgical evaluation according to clinical course.

conditions.diseaseMechanism: Antibiotic-mediated microbiome disruption permits toxigenic C. difficile expansion; toxin-mediated epithelial injury produces diarrhoea, colitis and potentially fulminant disease.

conditions.name: Complicated Intra-Abdominal Infection
conditions.summary: Early source control plus appropriate antimicrobial therapy are the core management principles.
before: Obtain blood cultures in septic patients
Obtain operative/peritoneal specimens when source control is performed
Assess whether infection is community- or hospital-acquired
Prioritise source control

recommendations.label: Principle
preferred: Use narrower therapy for community-acquired IAI when appropriate; hospital-acquired IAI more often requires MDR-aware coverage
alternative: Tailor to local epidemiology and culture
recommendations.duration: After adequate source control, duration should be limited and response-driven

recommendations.label: Complicated diverticulitis / appendicitis phenotype — national pathway
preferred: Non-sepsis: amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q6h OR ampicillin–sulbactam 1.5–3 g IV q6h
Sepsis / organ failure: piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6–8h
alternative: Non-sepsis: ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h OR cefoperazone 1–2 g IV q12h PLUS metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h
recommendations.duration: Complicated appendicitis: 4–7 days when adequate source control is achieved and recovery is rapid; reserve carbapenem for high AMR risk.
notes: If piperacillin–tazobactam is given q8h, NAG specifies extended infusion over 3–4 h.
Source control remains central.

conditions.name: Complicated Urinary Tract Infection
conditions.summary: HPUSM ASP 2025 gives a simple local empirical regimen for complicated UTI; resistance phenotype should redirect to the dedicated ESBL/AmpC/CRE pathway when present.
before: Obtain urine culture before antibiotics when feasible
Assess obstruction/stones and need for source control
Review previous urine cultures and recent antimicrobials
Check renal function

recommendations.label: Empirical
preferred: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q6h
alternative: Cefuroxime 750–1500 mg IV q8h
recommendations.duration: 10–14 days

recommendations.label: Complicated UTI
preferred: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q6–8h OR ampicillin–sulbactam 1.5–3 g IV q6h; may add an aminoglycoside when indicated
alternative: Cefuroxime 750–1500 mg IV q8h
Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h
Ceftazidime 2 g IV q8h
recommendations.duration: Usually 5–7 days; use site/source and clinical response to individualise.

why: Known ESBL/AmpC/CRE changes the preferred treatment and should not be handled by the uncomplicated empirical card.
conditions.diseaseMechanism: Structural/functional urinary abnormalities, devices or systemic illness increase the likelihood of resistant Gram-negative pathogens and failure without source control.

conditions.name: Cryptococcal Meningitis
conditions.summary: Induction, consolidation and maintenance phases must be distinguished; HIV/transplant status materially changes the pathway.
before: Confirm host context (HIV/transplant/non-HIV)
Measure and manage CSF opening pressure when appropriate
Check renal, hepatic, haematologic and electrolyte baseline before induction therapy

recommendations.label: Non-HIV / non-transplant — induction
preferred: Amphotericin B deoxycholate 0.7–1 mg/kg IV q24h + flucytosine 100 mg/kg/day PO in q6h divided doses
alternative: Use formulation/host-specific specialist regimen when toxicity or access changes the choice
recommendations.duration: Induction generally 4–6 weeks, then consolidation and maintenance phases.

recommendations.label: Consolidation / maintenance
preferred: Fluconazole 400–800 mg PO q24h for consolidation, then 200 mg q24h maintenance
recommendations.duration: Consolidation ~8 weeks; maintenance duration depends on host context.

why: Control of intracranial pressure and phased antifungal therapy are both essential.
conditions.diseaseMechanism: Inhaled yeast can disseminate haematogenously to the CNS, especially with impaired cellular immunity; capsular burden and CSF outflow obstruction contribute to raised intracranial pressure.

conditions.name: Diabetic Foot Infection
conditions.summary: Classify infection severity, obtain deep tissue cultures when needed, and prioritise debridement/off-loading/vascular assessment.
before: Classify mild/moderate/severe infection
Assess osteomyelitis and perfusion
Obtain deep tissue rather than superficial swab when possible
Plan debridement/source control

recommendations.label: Mild
preferred: Cephalexin 500 mg PO q6h
alternative: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 625 mg PO q8h
recommendations.duration: 7–14 days in the local table; adjust to clinical response.

recommendations.label: Moderate–severe
preferred: Ampicillin–sulbactam 3 g IV q6–8h
alternative: Ceftazidime 2 g IV q6h if melioidosis is suspected in the local pathway
recommendations.duration: 7–14 days; deeper infection/osteomyelitis requires its own duration.

recommendations.label: National pathway
preferred: Use current NAG severity-based diabetic-foot pathway with culture/source-control integration
recommendations.duration: Severity/source-control dependent; check live NAG for the latest December 2025/Jan 2026-era pathway.

why: Antibiotics alone do not address ischaemia, necrosis or deep collections.

conditions.name: Disseminated / CNS Histoplasmosis
conditions.summary: Severe disseminated and CNS disease require amphotericin-based induction followed by prolonged itraconazole therapy.
before: Assess CNS involvement and disease severity
Check renal/electrolyte/hepatic baseline and major azole interactions

recommendations.label: Moderate–severe disseminated disease
preferred: Amphotericin B deoxycholate 0.7–1 mg/kg IV q24h or liposomal amphotericin B 3 mg/kg IV q24h for induction
alternative: Step down to itraconazole after clinical improvement
recommendations.duration: Induction generally about 2 weeks then itraconazole for ≥12 months.

recommendations.label: CNS histoplasmosis
preferred: Liposomal amphotericin B 5 mg/kg IV q24h induction, then itraconazole
recommendations.duration: Prolonged treatment, typically ≥12 months, specialist-directed.

why: CNS disease requires a different intensity/duration from uncomplicated pulmonary disease.

conditions.name: Disseminated Mycobacterium avium Complex Infection
conditions.summary: Combination therapy is mandatory to prevent resistance and treat disseminated MAC.
before: Confirm microbiologic diagnosis and HIV/immunocompromised status
Check interaction burden with rifamycins/macrolides

recommendations.label: Combination therapy
preferred: Clarithromycin 500 mg PO q12h + ethambutol 15 mg/kg PO q24h + rifampicin 10 mg/kg PO q24h
alternative: Amikacin may be added in selected severe disease under specialist guidance
recommendations.duration: Prolonged therapy guided by immune recovery and specialist criteria.

why: Macrolide monotherapy rapidly selects resistance.

conditions.name: Fournier Gangrene
conditions.summary: A surgical emergency: rapid debridement/source control is the priority alongside broad antimicrobial therapy.
before: Immediate surgical/urologic review and debridement planning
Blood and deep tissue cultures
Assess shock, renal failure and need for ICU support

recommendations.label: Empirical broad therapy
preferred: Piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6–8h + metronidazole when required by the source pathway
alternative: Carbapenem-based regimen when MDR/ESBL risk justifies it
recommendations.duration: Continue according to source control, microbiology and clinical response.

why: Antibiotics cannot compensate for delayed debridement in necrotising infection.

conditions.name: Healthcare-Associated Ventriculitis / Meningitis
conditions.summary: Device-associated CNS infection requires appropriate CSF cultures, antipseudomonal coverage, Gram-positive coverage when indicated, and device/source-control planning.
before: Obtain appropriate microbiology before antimicrobial therapy when this will not cause harmful delay
Review previous cultures and recent antimicrobial exposure
Check allergy, renal function and interacting/toxic co-medications
Assess source control and severity
Obtain CSF/device cultures if feasible
Assess infected EVD/shunt/device for removal or exchange with neurosurgical team

recommendations.label: Empirical healthcare-associated CNS infection
preferred: Ceftazidime 2 g IV q8h ± vancomycin when Gram-positive device pathogens are a concern
alternative: Meropenem 2 g IV q8h
recommendations.duration: Pathogen/device/source-control dependent; de-escalate once microbiology is available.

why: Healthcare-associated CNS pathogens differ from community meningitis and device management may determine cure.

conditions.name: Helicobacter pylori Infection
conditions.summary: Use the current NAG eradication regimen rather than combining antibiotics ad hoc; local resistance and prior macrolide exposure matter.
before: Confirm indication for eradication therapy
Review prior macrolide/metronidazole exposure and allergy

recommendations.label: Eradication therapy
preferred: Use the current NAG multidrug eradication regimen; clarithromycin-containing therapy uses clarithromycin 500 mg PO q12h where appropriate
alternative: Choose the NAG alternative regimen when resistance/exposure/allergy makes clarithromycin-based therapy unsuitable
recommendations.duration: Use the duration specified in the current NAG H. pylori section.

why: Eradication success depends on the complete regimen, acid suppression and resistance pattern.
conditions.diseaseMechanism: Persistent gastric colonisation is enabled by urease, motility and mucosal adherence; chronic inflammation contributes to ulcer disease and gastric neoplasia risk.

conditions.name: High-Risk Febrile Neutropenia
conditions.summary: High-risk patients need rapid antipseudomonal therapy after blood cultures; vancomycin is not routine unless a defined Gram-positive indication exists.
before: Obtain blood cultures promptly
Give first antipseudomonal dose within 1 hour in high-risk infection
Assess haemodynamic stability and focal source
Review prior colonisation/resistance and prophylaxis

recommendations.label: Initial high-risk regimen
preferred: Piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6h; may add amikacin in severe sepsis according to NAG
alternative: Cefepime 2 g IV q8h ± amikacin; add metronidazole for selected severe mucositis/intra-abdominal/perianal/colitis contexts
recommendations.duration: Generally minimum 5–7 days or until clinical criteria permit stopping; tailor to cultures and neutrophil recovery.

recommendations.label: Severe sepsis / persistent deterioration
preferred: Meropenem 1 g IV q8h ± vancomycin when a defined MRSA/catheter/SSTI/shock indication exists
alternative: Imipenem/cilastatin source-specific severe regimen ± vancomycin
recommendations.duration: Reassess and de-escalate; stop empiric vancomycin after 48 h if no Gram-positive evidence.

conditions.name: Hospital-/Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia
conditions.summary: Treat as a syndrome with acquisition timing, MDR risk, respiratory sampling and rapid 48–72 h reassessment. Do not interpret a positive respiratory culture without clinical context.
before: Obtain appropriate cultures before antimicrobials when this does not cause harmful delay
Review previous microbiology and recent antimicrobial exposure
Check allergy and previous serious antimicrobial adverse reactions
Check renal function and whether renal replacement therapy is being used
Obtain a good-quality endotracheal aspirate/non-invasive respiratory specimen when possible
Assess need for MRSA and MDR Gram-negative coverage using local epidemiology

recommendations.label: Early onset (2–4 days)
preferred: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q8h
alternative: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h
recommendations.duration: 7 days

recommendations.label: Late onset (≥5 days)
preferred: Piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q8h ± vancomycin 15–20 mg/kg q8–12h
alternative: Cefepime 2 g IV q8h ± vancomycin 15–20 mg/kg q8–12h
recommendations.duration: 7 days

recommendations.label: No MDR risk factors
preferred: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q8h OR ceftriaxone 1 g IV q12h
alternative: Cefepime 2 g IV q8h OR piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6h
recommendations.duration: 7 days

recommendations.label: MDR risk factors — Gram-negative coverage
preferred: Cefepime 2 g IV q8h OR piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6h
alternative: Meropenem 1 g IV q8h OR imipenem 500 mg IV q6h when clinically appropriate
recommendations.duration: 7 days

recommendations.label: Specific MDR phenotype
preferred: ESBL: meropenem/imipenem; MRSA: vancomycin; CRAB/CRE require phenotype-directed therapy
alternative: Use dedicated MDR guidance and susceptibility results
recommendations.duration: Usually 7 days; longer only for delayed response or specific complications

recommendations.label: Early onset (2–4 days)
preferred: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q8h
alternative: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h
recommendations.duration: 5–7 days; adjust to local antibiogram and broaden only if clinical deterioration requires it.

recommendations.label: Late onset / severe / Pseudomonas risk
preferred: Piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6–8h OR cefepime 2 g IV q8h
alternative: High MDR risk: meropenem 1 g IV q8h OR imipenem/cilastatin 500 mg IV q6h
recommendations.duration: 7 days; de-escalate to culture/susceptibility. Piperacillin–tazobactam q8h should be infused over 3–4 h.

why: MDR risk factors materially change empirical coverage.
MSIC notes Acinetobacter, Klebsiella pneumoniae and Pseudomonas aeruginosa among common ICU isolates in the cited MRIC report.
Aim for ≤7 days in uncomplicated response and de-escalate with microbiology.
conditions.diseaseMechanism: Hospital/ventilator exposure, impaired airway defences, aspiration/microaspiration and biofilm on airway devices permit lower-respiratory infection; prior antibiotics and colonisation select resistant flora.

conditions.name: Infected Pancreatic Necrosis / Infection in Acute Pancreatitis
conditions.summary: Routine antibiotic prophylaxis is not indicated in sterile acute pancreatitis; treat proven/suspected infection with source-control planning.
before: Distinguish sterile inflammation from infected necrosis or extra-pancreatic infection
Obtain cultures during drainage/source-control procedure when feasible

recommendations.label: Sterile acute pancreatitis
preferred: No routine prophylactic antibiotic
recommendations.duration: Not applicable.

recommendations.label: Infected necrosis / extra-pancreatic infection
preferred: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h OR cefotaxime 2 g IV q8h are source-listed options in selected contexts
alternative: Escalate based on microbiology, severity and local resistance when necessary
recommendations.duration: Source-control and response driven.

why: Fever and inflammation in pancreatitis do not by themselves prove infection.

conditions.name: Infective Endocarditis
conditions.summary: Empirical therapy depends on native vs prosthetic valve and must be narrowed to organism-specific treatment when cultures are available.
before: Obtain at least 2 sets of blood cultures before antibiotics when feasible
Clarify native vs prosthetic valve and timing of valve surgery
Assess for heart failure, embolic/metastatic infection and need for echocardiography
Check renal function before aminoglycoside/vancomycin-containing regimens

recommendations.label: Native valve — empirical, culture pending
preferred: Ampicillin 2 g IV q4h PLUS gentamicin 3 mg/kg IV q24h PLUS/MINUS cloxacillin 2 g IV q4h
alternative: Penicillin allergy: vancomycin 15–20 mg/kg IV q8–12h PLUS gentamicin 3 mg/kg IV q24h
recommendations.duration: Source table lists 28–42 days depending on organism; definitive duration must follow organism/valve-specific guidance.

recommendations.label: Prosthetic valve — empirical, culture pending
preferred: Vancomycin 15–20 mg/kg IV q8–12h PLUS gentamicin 3 mg/kg IV q24h PLUS rifampicin 300–450 mg PO q12h
recommendations.duration: Definitive duration depends on organism and prosthetic-valve context.

recommendations.label: Prosthetic valve <12 months — empirical
preferred: Vancomycin 15–20 mg/kg IV q12h PLUS gentamicin 3 mg/kg IV q24h PLUS rifampicin 300–450 mg PO q12h
alternative: Optional cefepime 2 g IV q8h OR piperacillin/tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6h when non-HACEK Gram-negative coverage is indicated by local epidemiology
recommendations.duration: Narrow promptly to pathogen-specific treatment.

recommendations.label: Native valve — empirical
preferred: Ampicillin 2 g IV q4h + gentamicin 3 mg/kg IV q24h; may add cloxacillin 2 g IV q4h when S. aureus is suspected
alternative: Antibiotic allergy: vancomycin 15–20 mg/kg IV q8–12h + gentamicin 3 mg/kg IV q24h
recommendations.duration: Adjust promptly to culture/susceptibility; culture-negative cases warrant ID review.

why: Blood cultures before treatment are central to pathogen-directed therapy.
Aminoglycoside/vancomycin regimens require toxicity monitoring and should be narrowed when cultures permit.

conditions.name: Infective Exacerbation of COPD
conditions.summary: Antibiotics are for purulent infective exacerbations/ventilated patients; Pseudomonas risk changes therapy.
before: Confirm infective features and sputum purulence
Review prior sputum cultures and Pseudomonas history
Assess severity/need for ventilation
Check allergy and renal function

recommendations.label: Inpatient
preferred: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q8h; may add azithromycin 500 mg IV/PO q24h for 3 days
alternative: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h; may add azithromycin
recommendations.duration: 5–7 days

recommendations.label: Inpatient with Pseudomonas risk
preferred: Piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6–8h; may add azithromycin
alternative: Cefepime 2 g IV q8h; may add azithromycin
recommendations.duration: 7 days; q8h piperacillin–tazobactam should be infused over 3–4 h.

why: Do not prescribe antibiotics for every COPD exacerbation; purulence plus clinical criteria/ventilation drives antimicrobial use.

conditions.name: Influenza in Hospitalised / Severe Illness
conditions.summary: Treat influenza with antiviral therapy when indicated; antibacterial therapy is only for suspected/confirmed bacterial co-infection.
before: Obtain influenza testing when available without delaying indicated antiviral therapy
Assess bacterial co-infection separately

recommendations.label: Influenza A/B
preferred: Oseltamivir 75 mg PO q12h
alternative: Use source-specific alternative when oseltamivir cannot be used
recommendations.duration: Commonly 5 days; severe/immunocompromised disease may require individualisation.

recommendations.label: Current national influenza pathway
preferred: Use current NAG antiviral pathway for hospitalised/severe influenza
recommendations.duration: Check live NAG because respiratory guidance is periodically updated.

why: A positive influenza diagnosis does not itself justify antibiotics.

conditions.name: Invasive Candidiasis / Candidaemia
conditions.summary: Haemodynamic status, prior azole exposure, Candida species/susceptibility and metastatic complications determine initial therapy and duration.
before: Obtain blood cultures
Assess for source/device removal
Assess haemodynamic stability and prior azole exposure
Evaluate for metastatic complications when candidaemia confirmed

recommendations.label: Stable / azole-susceptible context
preferred: Fluconazole: day 1 800 mg then 400 mg q24h in selected stable patients with susceptible Candida and no prior azole exposure
alternative: Echinocandin for haemodynamic instability, prior azole exposure or non-albicans risk
recommendations.duration: Uncomplicated candidaemia: 14 days from first negative blood culture; metastatic disease requires longer site-specific therapy.

conditions.diseaseMechanism: Barrier disruption and dysbiosis allow Candida translocation or device-associated bloodstream entry; deep-seated disease may occur without persistent candidaemia.

conditions.name: Invasive Mould / Fungal Infection — Drug Reference Hub
conditions.summary: This hub links source-supported antifungal monographs; definitive syndrome choice should follow microbiology, host status, site and dedicated fungal guidance.
before: Identify host risk and likely fungal syndrome
Obtain fungal microbiology/antigen/imaging where indicated
Review major azole interactions and organ dysfunction

recommendations.label: Voriconazole pharmacokinetic reference
preferred: Use syndrome-specific antifungal guideline; MSIC provides voriconazole loading/maintenance and renal formulation guidance
recommendations.duration: Syndrome-specific.

why: Antifungal choice cannot be inferred from a positive colonisation result alone.

conditions.name: Leptospirosis
conditions.summary: Both HPUSM and MSIC provide Malaysian treatment regimens. Their steroid statements are not identical and are therefore shown separately.
before: Assess organ involvement and severity, including AKI, respiratory failure, hypotension and arrhythmia
Send appropriate diagnostic testing without delaying treatment when clinical suspicion is high
Check renal and hepatic function

recommendations.label: Mild
preferred: Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h for 5–7 days
alternative: Azithromycin 500 mg PO q24h for 3 days
recommendations.duration: 5–7 days depending on regimen

recommendations.label: Moderate to severe
preferred: Benzylpenicillin 1.5 million units IV q6h
alternative: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h
recommendations.duration: 7 days
notes: HPUSM source states to add steroid for all severe leptospirosis.

recommendations.label: Severe disease
preferred: Benzylpenicillin 1.5 million units IV q6h OR ceftriaxone 1 g IV q12h
recommendations.duration: 7 days
notes: MSIC source states there is insufficient evidence to support routine corticosteroids in pulmonary haemorrhage.

recommendations.label: Mild disease
preferred: Azithromycin 500 mg PO q24h for 3 days OR doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h for 5–7 days OR amoxicillin 500 mg PO q8h for 7 days
recommendations.duration: Regimen-specific

recommendations.label: Mild adult disease
preferred: Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h for 5–7 days OR amoxicillin 500 mg PO q8h for 7 days
alternative: Azithromycin 500 mg PO q24h for 3 days; amoxicillin/azithromycin are pregnancy options in the NAG pathway
recommendations.duration: 5–7 days depending on regimen.

recommendations.label: Moderate / severe adult disease
preferred: Benzylpenicillin 1.5 million units IV q6h
alternative: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h
recommendations.duration: 7–10 days; corticosteroids are not routine solely for leptospirosis.

why: The source conflict on corticosteroid use is deliberately not reconciled by the app.
conditions.diseaseMechanism: Spirochaetal dissemination and endothelial/organ injury can cause AKI, jaundice, bleeding and pulmonary disease.

conditions.name: Lung Abscess / Empyema
conditions.summary: Antibiotics are only one component; drainage/source control is central when a pleural collection is present.
before: Obtain appropriate cultures before antimicrobials when this does not cause harmful delay
Review previous microbiology and recent antimicrobial exposure
Check allergy and previous serious antimicrobial adverse reactions
Check renal function and whether renal replacement therapy is being used
Obtain pleural fluid/pus culture where feasible
Arrange drainage for empyema/complicated collection

recommendations.label: Local lung abscess
preferred: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q6–8h
alternative: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h + metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h
recommendations.duration: 28–42 days in the source; step down when clinically improved

recommendations.label: Healthcare-associated aspiration/lung abscess
preferred: Piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g q6h OR cefepime 2 g q8h + metronidazole 500 mg q8h
alternative: Meropenem 1 g q8h OR imipenem 500 mg q6h
recommendations.duration: Lung abscess minimum 4 weeks; response/imaging dependent

recommendations.label: No recent thoracic procedure or HAP/VAP
preferred: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q6–8h OR ampicillin–sulbactam 3 g IV q6h
alternative: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h + metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h
β-lactam allergy: clindamycin 600 mg IV/PO q8h
recommendations.duration: After adequate source control: generally 2–4 weeks from drainage/surgery and defervescence; longer (4–6 weeks) if source control is inadequate.

recommendations.label: Post-procedure / concomitant HAP-VAP
preferred: Piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6–8h OR cefepime 2 g IV q8h + metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h; add vancomycin when indicated
alternative: Meropenem 1 g IV q8h; add vancomycin when indicated
recommendations.duration: Source-control dependent; generally 2–6 weeks.

conditions.name: Melioidosis
conditions.summary: MSIC describes a prolonged two-phase treatment strategy: an IV intensive phase followed by oral eradication therapy, with duration determined by infection site and severity.
before: Obtain cultures; culture is the diagnostic mainstay
Look for deep-seated abscesses and consider CT/ultrasound abdomen/pelvis in culture-positive disease
Assess need for drainage or surgical intervention
Check renal function and TMP-SMX contraindications/interactions

recommendations.label: Initial intensive phase
preferred: Meropenem 1 g IV q8h (2 g q8h for CNS infection) OR imipenem 500 mg IV q6h
alternative: Ceftazidime 2 g IV q6h
recommendations.duration: At least 2 weeks; longer for pneumonia with ICU admission/bacteraemia, deep collections, osteomyelitis, CNS or arterial infection.
notes: Optional TMP-SMX is added in selected sites such as cutaneous disease, osteomyelitis, septic arthritis, CNS infection and deep collections in the cited guide.

recommendations.label: Duration framework
preferred: Intensive-phase duration and eradication-phase duration are site-specific; the cited table ranges from 2 to 8 weeks intensive therapy and 3 to 6 months eradication therapy for many listed foci.
recommendations.duration: Use the site-specific melioidosis duration table.

recommendations.label: Intensive therapy — mild/moderate non-neurological
preferred: Ceftazidime 2 g IV q6h
alternative: Escalate to carbapenem pathway for severe disease/clinical indication
recommendations.duration: Intensive-phase duration is site/severity dependent; check current NAG pathway and subsequent eradication phase.

recommendations.label: Severe / septic shock / neurological
preferred: Severe persistent bacteraemia or severe sepsis: meropenem 1 g IV q8h OR imipenem/cilastatin source-specific high-dose regimen
Neuromelioidosis or septic shock requiring ICU support with augmented renal clearance: meropenem 2 g IV q8h
alternative: Add trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole for selected neurological, osteoarticular, genitourinary/prostatic, skin/soft-tissue, ocular or pericardial foci per NAG.
recommendations.duration: Site/severity dependent; de-escalate to ceftazidime once stable when appropriate.

why: Severe disease, deep infection and CNS/vascular involvement require longer treatment than uncomplicated infection.
conditions.diseaseMechanism: Environmental inoculation/inhalation/ingestion can lead to pneumonia, sepsis and multiple deep abscesses; intracellular persistence explains relapse risk and the need for eradication therapy.

conditions.name: Necrotising Fasciitis
conditions.summary: Surgical source control is time-critical. Antimicrobials should not delay debridement.
before: Urgent surgical review and debridement/source control
Blood cultures and deep operative tissue cultures
Assess shock and organ support requirements

recommendations.label: Local empirical regimen
preferred: Piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6–8h ± clindamycin 600–900 mg IV q8h
alternative: Ampicillin–sulbactam 3 g IV q6h
recommendations.duration: 7–14 days in the source; tailor to source control and clinical response

recommendations.label: National source-control principle
preferred: Immediate aggressive surgical debridement is the primary treatment; empirical antimicrobial therapy should be broad and then streamlined to intraoperative culture and susceptibility.
recommendations.duration: Duration is source- and response-dependent after adequate debridement.
notes: Repeated debridement may be required for source control.

conditions.name: Osteomyelitis
conditions.summary: HPUSM separates acute empirical treatment from chronic disease, where surgical debridement and tissue culture guide therapy.
before: Obtain appropriate deep/tissue cultures where feasible
Assess for surgical debridement/source control
Review prior microbiology, implants and chronicity

recommendations.label: Acute osteomyelitis
preferred: Cloxacillin 2 g IV q6h
alternative: Clindamycin 600 mg IV q8h
recommendations.duration: 2–4 weeks IV followed by oral therapy; total 6 weeks in the source table.

recommendations.label: Chronic osteomyelitis
preferred: Empirical treatment is not indicated; surgical debridement and tissue culture/susceptibility guide treatment.
recommendations.duration: Source table lists 6 weeks to 3 months depending on context.

recommendations.label: Acute osteomyelitis
preferred: Cloxacillin 2 g IV q6h; tailor to tissue/bone culture
alternative: Cefazolin 2 g IV q6–8h for appropriate β-lactam allergy context
recommendations.duration: Initial IV 2–4 weeks then oral therapy; minimum total 6 weeks, modified by response. S. aureus osteomyelitis with bacteraemia requires prolonged IV therapy.

why: Chronic osteomyelitis is a source-control and culture-directed problem rather than an empirical-antibiotic-only problem.

conditions.name: Pneumocystis jirovecii Pneumonia
conditions.summary: MSIC ICU provides pathogen-specific therapy for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia in severe community-acquired pneumonia pathways.
before: Confirm immunocompromised context and obtain appropriate diagnostic specimens where feasible
Check renal function, potassium and blood counts before high-dose trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole
Assess whether adjunctive corticosteroid criteria are met

recommendations.label: Preferred
preferred: Trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole 5 mg/kg (TMP component) IV q6–8h
alternative: Pentamidine 4 mg/kg IV daily OR primaquine 30 mg PO q24h PLUS clindamycin 600–900 mg IV q8h
recommendations.duration: 21 days

recommendations.label: Adult HIV-associated PJP/PCP — national pathway
preferred: Trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole 15–20 mg/kg/day (TMP component) IV/PO in 3–4 divided doses
alternative: Mild–moderate: clindamycin 600 mg IV/PO q8h + primaquine 30 mg base PO q24h; severe: pentamidine 4 mg/kg/day IV OR clindamycin + primaquine
recommendations.duration: 21 days; severe disease should receive adjunctive corticosteroid according to the NAG regimen.
notes: Consider IV→PO switch after clinical improvement because trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole and clindamycin have high oral bioavailability.
Check G6PD status before dapsone or primaquine.

why: High-dose TMP-SMX is weight-based on the trimethoprim component and requires toxicity monitoring.

conditions.name: Postpartum Endometritis
conditions.summary: Treat postpartum uterine infection with broad polymicrobial coverage and reassess for retained products/abscess if response is poor.
before: Obtain cultures when clinically indicated
Assess retained products and source-control need

recommendations.label: Empirical therapy
preferred: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q8h OR ampicillin–sulbactam 3 g IV q6h
alternative: Source-listed cephalosporin + metronidazole or clindamycin/gentamicin combinations when appropriate
recommendations.duration: Continue IV until clinically improved and afebrile for approximately 24–48 h, then reassess need for further therapy.

why: Failure to improve should trigger evaluation for retained products, abscess or another diagnosis.

conditions.name: Prosthetic Joint Infection
conditions.summary: Do not start routine empirical therapy before adequate cultures in a stable patient; treatment is culture- and surgical-strategy dependent.
before: Withhold empirical antibiotics in stable patient until appropriate specimens are obtained
Define surgical strategy: DAIR vs one-/two-stage revision/removal
Obtain multiple deep tissue cultures

recommendations.label: Culture-directed principle
preferred: Empirical treatment is not recommended before specimens; MSSA pathway uses cloxacillin + rifampicin when implant remains; MRSA pathway uses vancomycin + rifampicin.
alternative: Follow susceptibility and surgical plan.
recommendations.duration: Surgical strategy and organism determine duration.

recommendations.label: National culture-directed principle
preferred: Empirical treatment is generally not recommended before adequate cultures in stable prosthetic-joint infection.
alternative: For susceptible staphylococci with retained implant, rifampicin-containing combinations are used in source-specific pathways.
recommendations.duration: Typically prolonged and surgery-dependent; check current NAG orthopaedic section.

conditions.name: Pyogenic Liver Abscess
conditions.summary: Antimicrobial therapy must be paired with drainage/source control when indicated; sepsis shifts empiric breadth.
before: Obtain blood cultures before antibiotics when feasible
Obtain aspirate/drainage culture when procedure performed
Assess abscess size and need for drainage
Assess sepsis/organ failure and prior biliary instrumentation

recommendations.label: Non-sepsis
preferred: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q6h OR ampicillin–sulbactam 3 g IV q6h
alternative: Cefoperazone, ceftriaxone, cefotaxime or cefuroxime ± metronidazole according to anaerobic risk
recommendations.duration: 2–6 weeks; shorter with adequate drainage and fever resolution; step down when improving.

recommendations.label: Sepsis / organ failure
preferred: Piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6–8h
alternative: Use source-specific alternatives and resistance-risk assessment
recommendations.duration: 2–6 weeks; source-control dependent. q8h piperacillin–tazobactam is extended over 3–4 h.

why: Drainage/source control can shorten therapy and is part of definitive management.

conditions.name: Rickettsial Infection
conditions.summary: Doxycycline is the key first-line therapy for typical rickettsial disease; severe illness may require combination/source-specific treatment.
before: Review exposure/travel and organ dysfunction
Send appropriate serology/PCR when available without delaying treatment in strongly suspected severe disease

recommendations.label: Mild
preferred: Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h
alternative: Azithromycin 500 mg PO q24h
recommendations.duration: Doxycycline ~5 days; azithromycin ~3 days in the cited pathway.

recommendations.label: Moderate–severe
preferred: Azithromycin IV + doxycycline using the current NAG severe-disease regimen
recommendations.duration: IV to oral once clinically improved; complete the source-listed course.

why: Clinical response to doxycycline can be rapid, but severe organ involvement still requires ICU support and diagnostic confirmation.

conditions.name: Septic Arthritis
conditions.summary: Drainage/washout and culture-directed therapy are central; empirical therapy primarily targets S. aureus/streptococci in typical native-joint disease.
before: Obtain joint aspirate for cell count, Gram stain and culture before antibiotics if this does not delay urgent care
Obtain blood cultures in systemic illness
Arrange drainage/washout when indicated

recommendations.label: Native joint empirical — no specific Gram-negative risk
preferred: Cloxacillin 2 g IV q4–6h
alternative: Cefazolin 2 g IV q6–8h; clindamycin or vancomycin may be used in selected allergy/MRSA contexts
recommendations.duration: Typically 2–4 weeks IV then oral to complete 4–6 weeks, modified by organism/source control/response.

conditions.name: Septic Shock — Undifferentiated Empirical Antibiotic
conditions.summary: Use this only as an undifferentiated local starting reference. The final empirical regimen should be driven by suspected source, previous cultures, recent antibiotics and local resistance patterns.
before: Obtain blood cultures before antimicrobials if this does not delay treatment
Identify likely source and source control requirement
Review prior cultures/colonisation and recent antibiotics
Assess allergy, renal function and local resistance patterns

recommendations.label: Non-diabetic — undifferentiated local guide
preferred: Piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q8h
alternative: Source-directed therapy may supersede this
recommendations.duration: Revise/de-escalate at 48–72 h based on cultures and clinical source

recommendations.label: Diabetic — undifferentiated local guide
preferred: Ceftazidime 2 g IV q6–8h
alternative: Source-directed therapy may supersede this
recommendations.duration: Revise/de-escalate at 48–72 h

recommendations.label: Sepsis / septic shock — source-directed national principle
preferred: Give broad-spectrum empirical therapy directed at the most likely source and pathogens; incorporate prior microbiology, resistance risk/colonisation and local susceptibility data.
alternative: If source becomes apparent, switch to the source-specific NAG pathway rather than maintaining an undifferentiated regimen.
recommendations.duration: Reassess daily; modify/de-escalate at 48–72 h as microbiology and clinical trajectory clarify the diagnosis.

why: The MSIC ICU guide stresses rapid microbiological sampling, appropriate empirical coverage, PK/PD optimisation, source control and de-escalation.

conditions.name: Severe Community-Acquired Pneumonia
conditions.summary: Severe CAP requires severity assessment, atypical coverage when appropriate, and escalation to antipseudomonal therapy only when Pseudomonas risk is present.
before: Obtain appropriate cultures before antimicrobials when this does not cause harmful delay
Review previous microbiology and recent antimicrobial exposure
Check allergy and previous serious antimicrobial adverse reactions
Check renal function and whether renal replacement therapy is being used
Assess CAP severity (e.g. CURB-65/SMART-COP) and ICU need
Assess strong Pseudomonas risk and recent healthcare/antibiotic exposure

recommendations.label: Severe pneumonia (CURB65 >3)
preferred: Piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6–8h when Pseudomonas risk + azithromycin 500 mg IV/PO q24h
alternative: Use syndrome-/risk-specific alternative from local guidance
recommendations.duration: 5–7 days

recommendations.label: Severe CAP — usual pathogens
preferred: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q8h + azithromycin 500 mg IV q24h
alternative: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV q12h OR cefotaxime 2 g IV q8h + levofloxacin/moxifloxacin
recommendations.duration: Usually 5–7 days for β-lactam component; atypical duration varies

recommendations.label: If Pseudomonas risk
preferred: Cefepime 2 g IV q8h
alternative: Piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6h
recommendations.duration: 7 days

recommendations.label: Severe CAP — national 2026-updated pathway
